title: Function - Repetitive Calling
code:
def happy():
    print("Happy Birthday to you!")

def bday(name):
    happy()
    happy()
    print("Happy Birthday, dear {0}!".format(name))
    happy()

def main():
    bday("Mary")
    bday("Josh")
    bday("Professor Flynn")
main()

lines.explanation: Defining the function 'happy'. Here empty parenthesis states that no extra argument is passed.
Defining another function 'bday'. This function takes in the argument 'name'. Argument can be considered as input given to the function
This statement calls the function 'happy' inside of the function 'bday'. This will print out the contents of the 'happy' function
We can call a function multiple times
Printing out the message by passing the 'name' within the print statement.
calling the function 'bday' by passing the argument 'Mary'
calling the function 'bday' by passing the argument 'Josh'
calling the function 'bday' by passing the argument 'Flynn'

Calling the main function. So at a glance, the 'main' function is called, which then calls the 'bday' function by passing in the argument 'name' as a string. The bday function then in turn calls the 'happy' function
